stem: A vigorous plant has one flexible leader extending well above neighboring shoots. The goal is to reduce height and redistribute that shoot without intentionally removing tissue. Which response best matches the objective?
choices: Reposition and support the flexible leader into open canopy space, then monitor how growth redistributes
Remove lower lateral branches first, then keep the tall leader upright as the dominant shoot
Pinch or cut the leader repeatedly until its height matches neighboring shoots, then reassess the resulting canopy structure
Wait for the leader to stiffen, then bend it sharply once so later adjustment is less necessary
rationale: Low-stress training uses gradual positioning and support to alter architecture while minimizing deliberate tissue injury; subsequent growth should be reassessed before further intervention.
